November 2009 # **26****th** **October 2009 – 6****th** **November 2009** # **SHFE stocks hit five-year high; LME Asia stocks continue to rise** SHFE copper stocks rose 6,859t in the week ending 30th October, and a further 1,440t in the week ending 6th November. This took SHFE stocks to a fresh five-year high. Total stocks are now 104,275t. However, this second rise was less than many expected, and is unlikely to have a major influence on the market – in fact prices rose slightly. Chinese traders claim sentiment is being little affected by rises in exchange stocks, as they are dwarfed by the scale of ‘invisible’ Chinese stocks held elsewhere. In addition to recent rises in SHFE stocks, however, LME stocks have also been building, particularly in Asia. Since the beginning of August there has been a net stock increase in Asian stocks of 58,400t. Combined US and European LME stocks have risen by 45,050t during the same period. LME material in Asian warehouses is stock that might have otherwise been expected to go to China. The rise in Asian LME stocks has been particularly marked in the first few days of November; net stocks are up 7,350t, which is more than half of the stock rise seen in this region during the whole of October. Subsequently, the SHFE 3-month copper price reached RMB 51,860/t on 26th October, which is the highest level in 2009 and the market contango moved to RMB300/t. Prices have since traded in a RMB 50,000-52,000 range. We believe that the significant fundamental lag is the main restriction that will prevent the copper price from continuing to rise in the short term. There is little evident support for the copper price climbing, either from the fundamental side or from the macro economy side in the near term, and exchange stocks continue to build. # **Spot concentrates market remains quiet** There has been very little activity in the spot concentrates market in China recently. The latest deal heard from market sources was at a low level of $10-15/1-1.5¢, which we believe may have been due to shipments being delayed at ports due to Chinese customs activity. Traders have offered zero quotation deals to smelters in the hope that they will accept the terms in order to procure supply, but there has been little interest from smelte

rs.  It appears that large smelters are currently able to maintain a good level of production (as shown in Q3 results) with raw materials purchased through already contracted purchases. Furthermore, CRU suspect that the easing of copper blister and scrap availability has also improved raw material supply.  As a result, Chinese smelters can maintain a high level of copper production without resorting to the spot concentrates market. 

# **Pessimistic expectations from China smelters for upcoming annual TC/RC negotiations** 

Regarding the upcoming annual TC/RC negotiations some Chinese smelters hold pessimistic views. They suspect the annual TC/RC may be settled at $45-50/4.5-5¢.  A deficit in the concentrates market and Chinese smelting overcapacity is the difficult reality, although domestic smelters may be reluctant to accept such terms.  Potential collectively agreed maintenance shutdowns are unlikely to have much positive impact for TC/RC negotiations.  If there is no repeat of the long-running positive arbitrage for cathode between SHFE and the LME which emerged in 2009, especially in the first half, and if sulphuric acid prices stay subdued, many Chinese smelters will struggle to survive. Therefore, we believe TC/RCs have limited scope to fall further. 

# **Spot cathode premium shows modest rebound** 

After a dreary period, the spot market for imported cathode has shown a modest recovery recently.  The premium for imported copper cathode is now $40-70/t. The premium for imported SXEW cathode is quoted at $30-40/t.  Along with the climb in the copper price, some consumers have shown more interest in buying, especially for long term shipment.  But we believe both supply and demand sides would like to wait.  For buyers they will wait for more obvious signs of the copper price trend.  Whilst for traders, if they can afford storage fees, they would prefer to sell their goods later given the positive annual premium outlook and current contango market.  Consequently, we suspect there will not be many spot imported cathodes deals happening before the annual premium negotiations are concluded.

# **Domestic smelters may benefit from copper blister import tax adjustment** 

According to Chinese customs, China will cancel its 17% value-added tax on the gold content of copper blister imports starting on 1<sup>st</sup> November.  We believe that domestic smelters will derive some small benefit from this policy adjustment.  It will allow Chinese smelters scope to widen their choice of raw material purchases away from a currently tight copper concentrate market and volatile scrap availability. Moreover, domestic copper smelters may reduce their copper blister purchase cost.  If imported copper blister includes a high gold content, companies currently have to pay tax on it, thereby reducing or eliminating their profit.  In the first nine months of 2009

, Chinese imports of copper blister and anode rose by 16.6% y o y to 161,855t. Chile, Zambia and the DRC are the main sources of imported blister. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **John Tomlinson (London):** +44 20 7903 2103 john.tomlinson@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 6th November 2009.
